## Teaching points

1. Check mentation and temperature to distinguish heat exhaustion from heat stroke. Reassess after cooling and hydration before discharge.
2. Altered mental status raises concern for heat stroke even if a later temperature is lower after cooling.
3. The scripted falling temperature assumes the already documented removal from heat. Confirm recovery, oral intake and safe supervision before discharge; avoid an immediate return to training.
